name: Unainuman
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, unclassifiable Brazilian language; Glottolog cites no descriptive references at all.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record unai1234 'Unainuman' (Unclassifiable; Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less; refs: Zamponi 2020 ms, Adelaar & Brijnen 2014, Kann 1989).

sources.note: Nothing on Unainuman stress. p.338: 'Other languages for which no affiliation or identification could be found so far are Cararí … and Unainuman (possibly Vuainuman), from a tributary of the river Iça … The Unainuman list is rather incomplete'. pp.339-340 discuss Natterer's diacritics generally (acute on é sometimes marks a central vowel in Bororo, not stress; hiatus = glottal stop) — no per-language accent statement.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center (held scanned text); Martius 1867 Beiträge II (held); Aikhenvald 1999 in Dixon & Aikhenvald, The Amazonian Languages (held text).

sources.note: Checked only to separate identities: these treat Spix/Martius/Wallace 'Uainumá' (= Uainuma-Mariate, uain1239, Arawakan), not Natterer's Unainuman list; nothing on stress for either.

sources.citation: Natterer, Johann. 1817-1835 (ms.). Wortlisten von Indianersprachen in Brasilien. Universitätsbibliothek Basel, UBH T 2 (e-manuscripta doi:10.7891/e-manuscripta-128842). Section no. 59 'Sprachproben der Nation Unainuman aus dem Rio Pa…[?] der in den R. Iça sich ergießt', ms. fol. 262-265 (IIIF canvases [761]-[768]; archive.org item natterer-wortlisten leaf index 760-767).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. It is a bare elicitation list: ca. 40 filled slots of Natterer's questionnaire (e.g. Teufel 'o ipé', Vater 'go ãn', Mann 'maa tschu', Kopf 'maãn schú', Hand 'mãn ũn', Sonne 'Coátü', Wasser 'okotschó', Taube 'okótschó', Papagei 'tanga', Messer 'nönnö'), with an acute accent on a handful of forms and short ethnographic remarks ('haben kein' for canoe, 'wusste nicht zu zählen' for numerals, closing note fol. 265). No remark on accent or pronunciation anywhere in the section.

sources.citation: Zamponi, Raoul. forthcoming (ms. 2020, 121 pp.). Extinct isolates, unclassified languages, and small families. In Patience Epps & Lev Michael (eds.), Amazonian Languages: An International Handbook. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Glottolog's top reference for unai1234; summarises what can be said about Unainuman from Natterer's data (7 pp. per Glottolog); might retranscribe the forms with accents. Unlikely to contain a stress rule but is the modern survey of record.

sources.note: The only scholarly edition of Natterer's list 59 'Unainuman'; its introduction on Natterer's notation/diacritics and the annotations to this list are the only place a remark on what his acute accents mean for this language could appear. Would supersede everything else.

sources.citation: Kann, Peter. 1989. Die ethnographischen Aufzeichnungen in den wiederentdeckten Wortlisten von Johann Natterer, während seiner Brasilienreise zwischen 1817-1835. Archiv für Völkerkunde 43: 101-146.
